sections.overview: The Bat Hawk is a raptor of sub-Saharan Africa and parts of South and Southeast Asia, including New Guinea.
sections.identification: It has dark plumage, large yellow eyes and an unusually wide gape; adults are about 41–51 cm long.
sections.habitat: It uses forests, savannas and wooded areas near towns where flying prey is available.
sections.diet: Small bats make up much of its diet, supplemented by birds and large insects.
sections.behavior: It hunts mainly around dusk, catching prey on the wing near roosts or water, and can also forage at dawn or by moonlight.
sections.reproduction: Breeding seasons differ across its range, and the nest is a stick platform placed in a tall tree.
sections.ecology: Its foraging depends strongly on concentrations of flying prey, especially bats leaving roosts, so it may also hunt near artificial lights.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern. A South African regional assessment classified the local population as Endangered.
